title: Explore a concern, one step at a time.
intro: This short guide offers educational possibilities to read about. It cannot determine what condition you have.
disclaimer: This symptom checker is for education only and cannot diagnose a condition. For persistent, worsening, painful, or rapidly spreading symptoms, consult a qualified dermatologist.

stepThree.title: Topics you could explore
stepThree.intro: The examples below are not a diagnosis or ranked by likelihood. Many conditions overlap in appearance; only an appropriate clinical assessment can clarify your concern.
stepThree.context: Your answers are a reflection aid only. They have not been used to identify a condition or calculate a probability.
stepThree.urgent: Please seek prompt medical advice for painful inflammation, pus, rapidly spreading symptoms, or rapid hair loss. If symptoms are severe or you feel unwell, seek urgent care.

results.skin: An educational possibility: eczema or contact dermatitis can involve irritation. Psoriasis or other causes may also deserve discussion. Read the condition guides and seek an assessment if symptoms persist.
results.acne: An educational possibility: acne can involve pimples, but similar-looking bumps can have other causes. A dermatologist can discuss skin care and suitable treatment approaches.
results.pigment: An educational possibility: melasma is one cause of uneven pigmentation; other changes can look similar. Sun protection and a professional assessment are useful topics to discuss.
results.hair: An educational possibility: pattern hair loss, telogen effluvium, or alopecia areata may be worth reading about. These are different conditions and cannot be distinguished by this guide.
results.scalp: An educational possibility: dandruff or seborrheic dermatitis may involve flakes. Scalp psoriasis and other concerns can also look similar; an assessment can help clarify next steps.
results.other: An educational possibility: your concern may relate to a range of skin or hair changes. Browse the library, note what you have noticed, and discuss it with a qualified dermatologist.
